_comment: A connector is DATA, never code. It says how to read a file, never WHERE that file is - the human picks it. Every token below is a literal; the line shape is the NAME of one this package implements. Nothing here is evaluated.
_verified: NOT MEASURED. Written 2026-09-16 against the documented and widely reported Android shape. A BELIEF, like its iOS sibling, and for the same reason: no native export existed on this machine.
_whySeparate: Same app, different line. Android writes '15/08/2026, 16:55 - Name: text' - no brackets, no seconds, a dash between stamp and sender. A connector may not carry an alternation (that would be a pattern, and a pattern from a stranger is a machine that hangs on somebody else's computer), so the two shapes are two connectors over one reader.
_fileName: The file is named after the conversation ('WhatsApp Chat with Débora.txt'), which is why filePattern matches the extension rather than a name.

chatLog._mediaWhy: BELIEF: Android writes '<Media omitted>' in English and a localised equivalent elsewhere. A caption rides behind the marker, so these are prefixes.
chatLog._selfWhy: Empty for the same reason as the iOS sibling: a native export writes the account's display name like any other participant and marks nobody as the self. Every turn comes back 'unknown' and the app asks once.
chatLog._dateOrderWhy: NOT declared. It follows the phone's locale; the reader resolves it from the file or says it could not.

_mark: No vendor asset ships on this machine to trace, and drawing a lookalike under WhatsApp's name would be a fabricated brand asset.
